summary: Branch DNS search/suffix truncation causes presigned hostnames to be rewritten, resulting in selective shard 403s
description:
Issue summary: Customer VelaCommerce reports intermittent 403s when Redwood serving nodes attempt to fetch large model shard ranges (presigned S3 URLs) from within their private deployment (VPCE). Failures are selective: small artifact fetches succeed, full-object GETs succeed from some subnets, but parallel ranged requests for large shards return AccessDenied (403) from the presigned host.

Impact: Production inference jobs for VelaCommerce intermittently fail to initialize large models. Customers see ~2-6% of shard range requests returning 403 which causes retry storms and increased token/compute cost. Affects only the private deployment in us-east-1.

Environment: Private deployment (customer-managed VPC) using VPCE to access S3-backed artifact store. Serving nodes run our 2026.02 runtime. Problem reproduces from two branch office subnets behind the customer's recursive DNS appliances; not reproducible from VelaCommerce's bastion that uses cloud DNS directly.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) From a node in the affected branch office subnet, curl a presigned shard GET (with Range header) -> observe 403 from S3-like endpoint
2) Re-run curl with the fully-qualified host name suffixed by a trailing dot (e.g., 'bucket.s3.amazonaws.com.') -> request succeeds
3) Re-run curl from same node but force resolver to 8.8.8.8 -> request succeeds
4) From a different customer subnet (same VPC) where DNS is resolved by corporate forwarding bypass -> requests succeed normally
observed_behavior: 403 AccessDenied for ranged GETs to presigned hostname only when resolved via the customer's branch recursive DNS/resolver appliance. S3 logs show the request reached a different backend hostname (internal ALB) and AccessDenied reason: 'Signature does not match' along with an altered Host header in some traces.
expected_behavior: Presigned shard range GETs should succeed from any customer subnet that can reach the artifact endpoint via the VPCE; DNS resolution should return the canonical S3 host used to generate the presigned URL, and host header should match the signed hostname.
logs: Serving node logs (excerpt): GET /shard?id=... Range: bytes=0-10485759 -> 403 AccessDenied (request-id: 5D1A9X)
S3-like endpoint audit: request-id 5D1A9X -> Host header received: 'bucket.s3.amazonaws.com.corp.local' -> Auth failed: Signature mismatch
tcpdump from branch node: DNS A lookup for 'bucket.s3.amazonaws.com' returns 52.216.xx.xx; subsequent DNS resolve with search suffix appended returns 10.1.2.7 (internal) via split-horizon resolver
investigation_notes:
Initial triage: reproduced from customer's branch subnets. Bypassing the corporate DNS (using 8.8.8.8 or adding trailing dot to the FQDN) returns the original public S3 hostname and fixes fetches.

Hypothesis: Customer's recursive resolver applies search-suffix aggregation incorrectly for single-label or multi-label FQDNs due to ndots and search order config. When the presigned host is queried without trailing dot, the resolver appends the corporate search suffix and returns a CNAME/A pointing into the customer's internal realm (10.*) or to a private ALB backed by their VPCE. Because presigned URLs are host-bound (signature includes hostname), routing to the internal backend produces signature mismatch and 403.

We observed that only ranged requests (multipart/range GETs) were failing in larger volumes; preliminary theory is that parallel ranged GETs cause different underlying connections to be routed to different backends due to split-horizon last-mile NAT or egress load-balancer rules, which amplifies the problem (some parts hit the correct endpoint, others hit the internal rewrite), causing partial shard failures and validation errors in the runtime.
hypothesis: Resolver search-suffix + ndots misconfiguration at branch DNS appliances rewrites FQDNs into split-horizon internal names. VPCE still NATs/forwards traffic, but host header mismatch results in S3 returning 403. Parallel range requests increase exposure because some connections resolve to the wrong IP. Not a Redwood presigned URL bug but a network/DNS configuration issue at customer side that interacts badly with VPCE split-horizon and presigned host binding.
workaround: Short-term mitigations provided to customer: 1) Re-generate presigned URLs with a trailing dot in hostname (e.g., 'bucket.s3.amazonaws.com.') — most resolvers treat the dot as absolute and will not append search suffix. 2) Configure branch DNS appliances to set 'ndots' higher (>=5) or remove the search suffix for the VPC domain. 3) Add an explicit hosts entry on the affected nodes mapping the presigned host to the expected public S3 IPs (temporary, not recommended at scale). 4) Route artifact fetches from branch nodes through a bastion/proxy that uses cloud DNS (short term).
impact_mitigation_status: Customer applied workaround #4 (proxy through bastion) during business hours; artifact fetch success rate returned to ~99.8%. We've scheduled a follow-up with customer's network team to update resolver configs.
next_steps:
1) SRE to verify whether VPCE policy/logs show requests routed to internal ALB when DNS includes search suffix. (Assigned: Tomás)
2) Recommend long-term: customer to exclude presigned S3 host patterns from search-suffix application or update branch resolver firmware.
3) Engineering to add a short note in the Private deployment onboarding docs about presigned-hostname and ndots/search-suffix caveat. (Assigned: Docs/DevEx)
4) Track/close once customer confirms resolver change in a staging branch and we observe no presigned 403s for 48 hours.
resolution: Pending customer DNS configuration change. No platform code change required at this time. If customer cannot change resolver behavior, we will discuss SDK-level fallback patterns (append trailing dot when generating presigned URLs) as a compatibility option, documented and opt-in only.
